Title: Walking in Silence
Content: Going for a walk is `text(one)` of the best ways to keep your mind and body healthy. You exercise and strengthen your muscles. You breathe more deeply. Your heart beats faster. You get a chance to think and relax.

Some people who take regular walks bring their phones with them. Sometimes they talk to friends and family on the phone or send them text messages. Other times they listen to music as they walk. While these activities are common, some experts believe that walking in silence is healthier.
Silent walking, as it is now called, is nothing new. People have been doing this for `text(hundreds of years)`. Recently, however, silent walking and its effects have almost disappeared.
Turning Off the Noise and Focusing on Yourself

A few `text(years)` ago, a woman was told by her doctor that she should take a walk for `text(thirty minutes every day)`. The doctor also challenged the woman to walk in silence. She should walk without a phone or music to listen to. She shouldn’t walk with someone else or even a pet.

It was hard. She said that for the `text(first two minutes)` of walking, she had no idea what to do with herself. As she said, “It was just me, myself, and I.” After a few `text(minutes)`, she relaxed a little. Because she had no distractions, she could finally focus on her thoughts and reflections. She could also pay far more attention to everything around her. She could hear, smell, and see things that she likely would have missed if she had been distracted by her phone.

When she got back home, she went online and described what her walk had been like. She described how silent walking caused her to focus on things she would normally ignore. Word spread, and soon a new trend started.

Taking a walk in nature is a great way to practice a silent walk. You might hear a bird’s song or the chittering of a squirrel. You might smell flowers, see a spiderweb, or feel the breeze in your hair or sunshine on your skin. Silent walking causes your senses to feel all the amazing things in nature.

You can take a silent walk in the city, too. If you use your senses, you might hear people talking, smell fresh-baked bread from a nearby bakery, or see an amazing bike riding by. Silent walking even makes you safer. Without music, calls, or conversations to distract you, you can pay better attention to crossing the street or noticing traffic lights.

`text(One)` of the best parts of silent walking is that you can practice using your imagination. Instead of being distracted by other things, you can go into your mind and see what is there. You can think of a story you would like to read or write. You can make plans for spending time with a friend. You might be surprised what your imagination creates.
Next time you get ready to go for a walk,

:ibox:`1`. put on your most comfortable shoes,
`2`. grab a jacket,
`3`. be sure to bring an adult with you,
`4`. turn off any cell phones,
`5`. leave the headphones or earbuds at home, and
`6`. go outside with nothing more than your thoughts and your senses.
See what you can hear, see, and smell in your world. But shhh! Wait until you are back home to talk about it.
